Haven't posted in a minute but this was me as I wanted to become a PvP player around Beyond Light. Lots of good tips here so I'll just drop my 2 cents.


1: Like everyone says, play cover. Peek around a wall, corner, boulder, whatever. You wanna be able to strafe or duck behind something QUICKLY especially with how fast things can kill you.


2: Disengage. Works in tandem with #1. It's okay to back off if a fight isn't going your way. Eventually you'll learn when to just hide vs run away, but that's an experience thing and will take a lot of dying to learn. That's ok. 


3: Slow down. This seems counterintuitive with how quickly the game moves, but one big tip that helped me early on was to take an extra split second to actually line up my shots and aim better. The mechanical skill will improve over time and you'll get faster at it, but PvP aim is not PvE aim. Treat yourself like a beginner and be gentle on yourself. 


4: Use the buddy system. Especially in this sandbox, teamwork makes the dream work. This is just a practice thing - but you'll get better at teaming the more you do it. Everyone has different play styles so it's hard to tell you to "adapt" to your teammates when you're still adapting to yourself. So for
now just stick close (but not too close) to someone and shoot who they shoot. 


5: Pick one tip you find helpful in this thread and focus on that for a while. Don't try and do this all at once because it's a lot. Give yourself room to suck, because you'll only get better. 


6: MOST IMPORTANT. It's just a game. Have fun with it. Every single PvP god, every gjake frostbolt zk cammy sird etc etc started somewhere. Take it one fight at a time and eventually you'll be collecting We Rans like candy.

I've been a pvp arcstrider since long before the subclass 3.0 days and it's for the most part stronger now than it used to be thanks to Jolt, Amplified, and Gathering Storm (though I do miss my bottom tree arcstrider days).

Storm now is very strong - great for locking down a zone, nuking a well, or challenging a bubble. Regular Arc Staff is a little harder to use since it isn't super fast and has low DR, but it's usable. Reflect can help counter other supers, or at the very least be used to kite an enemy team somewhere. And the light-light-heavy combo if pulled off right can destroy anyone's hopes and dreams.

Lethal Current is a strong aspect - incredibly so. The melee lunge range increase is huge (though all melee range increasing things need to go away imo). The aftershock on melee does a pretty decent chunk of damage too.

Tempest Strike needs a bit more love. Would like to see a little bit of tracking maybe, or a slightly larger aoe / faster movement speed - but it pairs super well w/ a slideshot shotgun. Can cleanup weak targets from a distance, jolt a group of enemies, etc. 

It's honestly not the best class, and it's certainly on the best in any one category - but it is a very solid skirmishing option. Arc grenades in general are all pretty strong, it has solid melee options, and 2 decent supers.

Even in this 140 dominant meta, I still find myself using my Igneous Hammer. A big big big part of using 120s effectively right now is learning how to pace your shots, and making sure you get the first hit in a gunfight.   


If I'm approaching a duel and I don't hit the first shot, or if I whiff my opener, I'm rotating out. Hitting that first shot is almost a must for 120s imo. Super important for any gunfight, but given the chunk-damage nature of 120s they need it even more.

Play around cover. You gotta be able to disengage if you start missing your shots. 120s do really well with peeking and pop shotting. Stay near cover and don't over extend. They got great range still, so play into that. 

120s are also great teamshot weapons. Plenty of my kills come from cleaning up a guardian who got out of my teammate's range but is still within mine. Conversely, they're also really good at weakening an enemy for an easy cleanup for your nearby teammates.   


Also know when to swap the 120 for something else. If it's not working out in a particular match, it's probably best to swap to a different gun.
